institutionName: UiT The Arctic University of Norway

questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Academic opportunities

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: The research at the facility of my choice, the environment of the university, exploring the city and nature around the university, the institutions connected to the university.

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: It was fine, the housing and student oranization was straightforward with what I needed to do.

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: My supervisor here was friendly and helped me with moving in, even. My door needed to be fixed upon arrival but the housing organization was quick in helping. Other assistance regarding student ID and so on lacked a bit.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing through my host institution

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: On campus

questions.question: What options were available for on campus housing? *
questions.answer: Various types of dorms ranging from private rooms in big dormitries to more intimate apartment types.

questions.question: What options were available for meal plans or cooking facilities? *
questions.answer: No meal plan was provided, a shared kitchen is available for cooking and storing needs. For on-campus eating there are a number of canteens available with vegetarian options, too.

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living in on campus housing? *
questions.answer: Different dorms provide a wildly different experience in socialization and well-being. I think smaller dorms provide a better experience in regards to having more space per person, the housing being more homely, and people being less isolated.

What unexpected costs did you encounter? *
questions.answer: I didn't encounter unexpected costs.

questions.question: What items were more or less expensive than you expected? *
questions.answer: Groceries and alcoholic beverages are overall very expensive in Northern Norway. Also, different sorts of Arctic experiences are expensive.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: A very well eqipped gym with some free opportunities, multiple cultural opportunities in museums and all over the town - Sámi lead, Arctic traditions, norwegian traditions were all available to see and experience in some way. Social activities were available like game clubs, different organizations for interests like security, casual events like free waffles or other food. Especially with the dawn of the polar night with which LED 'sun' lamps were made available every morning with free coffee. Scientific events like lectures or workshops are very regular.

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: I would recommend any events with free food and coffee which there is a lot of. Also, the free yoga at the gym. The cultural activities, small hikes, lectures of different sorts are all very good.

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer: I'd recommend going on a hike nearby the city, catching the northern lights, going to Polaria, going to a sauna and swimming in the fjord, eating some traditional foods. There are also opportunities like boat tours and whale watching tours, though more expensive.

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: Very easy, as the language and culture is similiar to the danish culture.

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: I'd recommend making friends at courses, going on hikes and events organized by the university or the norwegian tourist org. and making converstaion there. Also, utilize the online platforms and whatsapp groups and just ask if people want to go on hikes or meet at events that you want to go to.

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: The people here are used to the climate and mountains here while exchange students are not, so it can be physically demanding at first. Also, as going out can be pretty expensive it can be hard to find people who want to do it.

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: I appreciate the culture of loving nature and embracing the climate with the darkness and snow it brings. People can be reserved but very friendly as well.

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer: Take iniative and talk to everyone you want to and they will appreciate it. Go to all the free events you can and stock up on the free food there, especially the waffles. Embrace the rough nature around the city and hike as much as possible.

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: No.

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: Overcoming academic challanges that were out of my control by myself was very rewarding. Also, making a life for myself and making friends in a different place. Being able to live a relatively normal life in a new place.

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: Academic misunderstandings regarding my thesis's question and scope was a massive set-back, and it was difficult to figure it out at a new university.

questions.question: Any other comments?
Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
